#39525. I Tested Pangram to See If It Can Really Detect AI-Generated Content Like It Claims

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1006 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

I Tested Pangram to See If It Can Really Detect AI-Generated Content Like It Claims

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1006 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We know it can be difficult for human beings to spot AI-generated content, but can detection software fare any better?
  • It has been revealed that you'll find arguments on both sides of the debate as to whether or not Pangram's claims stand up.
  • Proponents of Pangram would point to an ongoing reward offer—presently at $3,950—available to anyone who can find a pre-2019 (and pre-LLM) piece of writing that Pangram falsely flags as being AI-written.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We know it can be difficult for human beings to spot AI-generated content, but can detection software fare any better? Pangram is one of the leaders in the field, promising a "near-zero false positive rate" by looking at "subtle cues" in the writing, based on a training and feedback model comparing human-made content with the AI equivalent.

It has been revealed that you'll find arguments on both sides of the debate as to whether or not Pangram's claims stand up. After a short story was flagged by Pangram and then judged to be free from AI, the detection engine has been accused of bias against text from minority writers.

Proponents of Pangram would point to an ongoing reward offer—presently at $3,950—available to anyone who can find a pre-2019 (and pre-LLM) piece of writing that Pangram falsely flags as being AI-written. So far, the reward is unclaimed.

It has been revealed that as the AI detector has recently added AI image and video detection to its capabilities, it seemed a good time to put Pangram's analysis skills to the test for myself. Here's how it performed in the three different content types.

On the human side, I picked out 10 of my most recent articles for Lifehacker, known to be written by a person because I personally wrote them—in the traditional way, I fretted over word choices, went back and changed sentences, and accidentally left in a variety of typos that editors thankfully fixed.

For the AI content, I rotated between ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, and got the LLMs to write 10 articles with the same headlines and the same approximate number of words, for a tech-savvy audience. I even asked the AI apps to vary their language use, so that the output would "read less like an LLM has written it.".

Industry observers note that pangram's AI text detector lets you upload files, but to make the task a little harder, I copied and pasted all of the text into the online article, so it wouldn't be able to rely on any metadata included in the file. The scans got the correct result each and every time: Human-written text came back as 100% human, and AI-written text came back as 100% AI.

Recent findings suggest that what's more, Pangram was certain about its results. All of the human writing was marked as highly likely to be human, and the vast majority of the AI writing was marked as highly likely to have come from an LLM. There were only a handful of phrases or sentences across thousands of AI words that got a "medium" rather than a "high" ranking for AI.

Now, there have been some edge cases where Pangram has got it wrong—like a poem repeating the same six words thousands of times—but as far as this sample goes, it can't be faulted. Clearly, my writing is too idiosyncratic and too clunky to be confused for the smooth sheen of AI-produced prose.

To be fair, I do have another advantage over AI: I can actually test out devices and apps in a way that LLM bots can't. ChatGPT can't experiment with One UI 9 (at least not yet), though it can scrape the web for various experiments and tests that real people have done.

However, I was able to fool Pangram to some extent by alternating AI paragraphs with human-written paragraphs. The text was flagged as AI, but the percentage estimate was typically lower (20-25%) than what it actually was (around 50%). If you're offloading some but not all of your writing to AI, some of it might slip though as real.

Recent findings suggest that image and video detection is the latest string to Pangram's bow, so I sifted through my phone's photo and video library for some pieces of content to test the AI on. Again, I used copy and paste to get the files into Pangram rather than uploading them, to limit how much information the AI detector could get from metadata.

According to recent reports, again, all the human-made content was recognized as such, with a very high level of certainty—whether it was complicated crowd shots or simpler images of natural scenes. Presumably, there are even more signals to go off than there are with writing, including camera movements, colors, style, consistency, and composition.

Next up, I generated a few images and videos in Google Gemini and ChatGPT, requesting results that would look as photorealistic and "non-AI" as possible—the resulting files covered people, animals, and buildings. As before, I used copy, paste, and a few screengrabs to try and limit the metadata Pangram had access to.

Here, too, the AI identification was spot on, with all of the artificial content recognized as such, to a high level of confidence. This is perhaps not surprising: I think AI images and especially AI video still have more "tells" than AI writing, especially if you've seen a lot of it, so I wasn't expecting Pangram to fail here.

I did try experimenting with real photos that had a little bit of AI in them, what with tools like Gemini and ChatGPT now so good at image editing, as well as creating pictures from scratch. These were marked as "unsure" by Pangram, though to cut it some slack, only a small amount of the images were altered.

As with the text, the best way to beat Pangram's detection systems seems to be to include some AI embedded in human-made content. It will most likely still fail the "100% human" test, but the tests I ran revealed that Pangram is less certain in these cases, or underestimates the amount of AI there actually is.

Increase the level of AI, and the detection gets more reliable—but if you're only using AI for a small part of whatever it is you're making, it's less worthwhile using AI tools anyway. As far as these tests go, Pangram's claims about accuracy check out, making it a useful tool if you need to ensure something is AI-free.

Pokémon Gold Version and Pokémon Silver Version were first released back in 1999 as the first installments in the second generation of the beloved Pokémon franchise. Introducing 100 new species, they are often regarded as some of the most successful in Nintendo's history, and now, almost 30-years on, Gold and Silver are set to return in a stunning 2027 release.

In a recent development, throughout the events of Pokémon Gold & Silver, players will stumble across Legendary Beasts in the Johto region: Entei, Raikou, and Suicune. Now, to celebrate the ongoing 30th anniversary celebrations for the Pokémon franchise, they will return in three new releases which will change the Pokémon Trading Card Game for good.

We all remember first running into these Legendary Beasts in Pokémon Gold Version and Pokémon Silver Version, as they were known to be hard to find when they would exit battle with seemingly no warning. As such, when Pokémon Crystal released in 2000 as the third game in the generation, Suicune became a set encounter. Unfortunately, the same could not be remarked for Entei and Raikou, who continued to elude players for years to come.

Sources indicate that however, Entei, Raikou, and Suicune will be hard to avoid next year, as the Legendary Beasts will be heading to the Pokémon Trading Card Game thanks to three unique sets. This leak comes from PokéBeach, who claims that in Japan, Magma Heartbeat, Lightning Impact, and Aurora Ripples will be added to the game, with each being based on the three Legendaries.

Set to arrive in Japan on May 21, 2027, it is currently unclear if these brand-newly introduced sets will also be receiving an English launch. However, if they do, it is likely that all three sets will be combined as one for their international launch.

In a recent development, as PokéBeach shared, "These are confirmed to be the first sets of the new Pokémon ex★ series, which was teased at Worlds in August. We still don't know what the Pokémon ex★ mechanic will entail. Earlier this month, Creatures indirectly hinted the series would start in May 2027 when they confirmed that booster pack prices would increase at that time.".

Sources indicate that as of now, we do not know any further information about these upcoming Pokémon Trading Card Game sets, but it will be the first time in the card game's history that three sets will be releasing on the same day. As PokéBeach explained, "Traditionally, a new series debuts with dual sets. In English, we then get one combined set.".

So, this is indeed a major day for Pokémon Trading Card Game players, and we can only hope that Magma Heartbeat, Lightning Impact, and Aurora Ripples will also be released internationally at later dates.

According to recent reports, for now, Pokémon fans are gearing up for the beginning of Pokémon Gen 10 with the arrival of Pokémon Winds and Pokémon Waves some time in 2027. Whilst details remain scarce, it will be the next major revision for the franchise, and it is already shaping up to be the most ambitious yet, with a rumored 300+ new Pokémon being added to the roster.

#39519. Eight Hacks Every Tidal User Should Know

Eight Hacks Every Tidal User Should Know

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1370 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that I recently switched from Apple Music to Tidal, and I'm happy I made the change.
  • Download your playlist as a .txt file.
  • Double click "install certificates" in the folder that opens after installation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I recently switched from Apple Music to Tidal, and I'm happy I made the change. The main reason is AI-made music: Tidal has stricter AI filtering than any other major streamer. The second reason is audio quality. While all major music streaming services do basically the same thing, Tidal's focus has always been on streaming music at the highest possible quality. While other streaming services have more or less "caught up" in terms of pure sonic fidelity, Tidal still is better at getting that quality to your speakers, if you know a few tricks.

Download your playlist as a .txt file. You can do this directly from Apple Music under File>Library>Export Playlist. You can't from Spotify, but the free site Exportify will download any of your playlists as a spreadsheet file you can save.

Install Python on your system. Double click "install certificates" in the folder that opens after installation.

Download this script. Save it in the same file as your playlist.

In a recent development, run the script: (For Mac, open Terminal. For Windows, go to the Command prompt. Type python3 on a Mac or py on Windows.) Drag the script into the terminal window and press enter. It should ask you to drag your downloaded playlist into the window next.

In a recent development, sign in to Tidal. Hit "Approve" to give permission for Tidal to run the script.

Have a banana. The script is going to search for all the songs on your playlist and match them to Tidal's library, so it can take a little while. I tested it with a playlist from Apple Music with 2,397 songs. It took about 20 minutes and found 2,362 of my tracks, a 99% success rate.

Fix the leftovers: The program creates two separate text files for "orphans." One is songs it couldn't find and one is songs it might be worth double-checking manually.

If everything goes well, your large playlist should be available on Tidal.

Note: The script uses a community-created library to talk to Tidal, so it could stop working if Tidal changes things up.

Like most streaming services, Tidal has a "heart" button called "add to my collection." You can click on any track, album, or playlist to "like" and saved it. But Tidal also has a separate, somewhat mysterious "Save for Later" option that puts songs, albums, and playlists into a separate collection. There are a couple reasons for this. First, it keeps a running list of upcoming-to-you music waiting for you on a rainy day, and secondly, it (presumably) affects your recommendation algorithm differently. While Tidal isn't open about every detail of its recommendation algorithm, I assume "save for later" has less weight (if any) on your future recommendations than "add to my collection.".

Sources indicate that on Tidal, tracks that are 100% AI-generated get an "AI" badge, earn no royalties, and are never placed on a Tidal-curated playlist. People can flip a switch in Settings to either allow or disallow AI content, too. Simple, but there's a bit of nuance that goes beyond the on/off switch. You have to set the AI-toggle separately on each device you use Tidal on, even if it's the same account. I guess this is so I can listen to AI music in my car but not at my desk? Sadly, AI detection is not a science, so some AI-made, and partly AI-made, tracks may still get through.

If you're streaming music from a music app through Bluetooth, the output is automatically compressed to a lower quality, and your phone stays in charge, so a phone call or a notification can interrupt your music. But Tidal's Tidal Connect feature skips the middleman. Music streams directly from your wifi to your speaker and your phone becomes a remote control, so you can take a call, go for a walk, and even run out of phone battery and the music will keep playing.

Have an external device with Tidal Connect compatibility.

Make sure your speaker or other output device and phone or computer are on the same wifi network.

Pick your speaker on your wifi network.

Click the icon again to switch back to your phone.

In a recent development, plenty of wifi speakers don’t support Tidal Connect, so check before you buy. Tidal keeps the full list of supported devices on its site. There's everything there from WiiM Mini—a $99 small box that adds Tidal Connect to speakers you already own—to dCS components that cost more than a car.

Tidal Connect isn't the only way to get the highest quality audio from Tidal. You can go for an old school, wired path like I have. I play audio from my desktop and route it directly to a mixer via USB. Here's the set-up:.

Settings > Streaming > Audio Quality: Max.

Sound Output: choose your mixer as the output device instead of your computer’s speakers.

Exclusive Mode: On. It’s under Sound Output > More Settings. Tidal sends audio straight to the mixer at each track’s native sample rate, without your computer resampling it or mixing in system sounds.

Force Volume. It's in the desktop app next to Exclusive Mode, under Settings > Streaming > Sound Output > More Settings. Force Volume means Tidal will always output at the highest volume. You'll be controlling the actual volume from your mixer.

Set your levels with the mixer’s faders.

To check what your mixer can handle, look at its maximum sample rate:.

Mac: Open Audio MIDI Setup (in Applications > Utilities), click your mixer, and open the Format menu. The highest number listed is your ceiling.

Windows: Go to Settings > System > Sound, click your mixer, and look under Output settings > Format.

It has been revealed that my cheap-ass mixer tops out a 16-bit/48kHz which is CD quality, but not Tidal's top of 24-bit/192kHz, but at least I can control the EQ. Speaking of...

It's much cooler to turn dials than mess with computer settings. Tidal doesn’t have an equalizer, so if you’re using Tidal Connect or a wired connection, you'll need something to shape the sound. Here are some options:.

Industry observers note that your computer: System-wide EQ apps, like Equalizer APO on Windows or SoundSource on Mac, can adjust Tidal’s output. They don’t work with Tidal Connect though, which bypasses your computer’s audio processing.

Your speaker’s app: If you use a Tidal Connect speaker or streamer, it probably has a companion app for EQ.

A mixer or audio interface: Channel EQ knobs let you adjust bass, mids, and treble by hand, in real time.

Your speakers: Many powered speakers and studio monitors have low and high controls on the back.

A stereo receiver or amp: Old-school bass and treble knobs still work in 2026.

In a recent development, most of Tidal's catalog streams as "better-than-CD quality" FLAC files at every subscription tier, so you might be inclined to click "play music at highest quality on everything." but settings are only as good as the gear you're using, and there are times when lower quality is the right choice. Here's when to turn down the settings:.

When you're in your car: CarPlay and Bluetooth cut audio down to CD quality or less before it reaches your speaker, and with road noises, it usually doesn't matter anyway, so turn the streaming down to "High" instead of "Max." Or download your playlist before you leave, if you must have "as good as possible" audio.

It has been revealed that you have a data cap and are off wifi. Top quality audio requires huge file transfer, so set your mobile data to High or Low and save Max for wifi.

Your connection is spotty: To avoid buffering, a lower setting keeps the music playing.

Recent findings suggest that this isn't a universal hack, but some Android phones have microSD card slots, which can save you a lot of hassle if you're downloading a lot of audio files—an album at high quality might top 1GB, so having an external source will save you a ton of hassle. If your phone has a microSD card slot, go to Tidal's settings, find "download destination" and choose the memory card.

ScreenRant’s 2026/27 Winter TV Preview: An Exclusive Look At Over 50 Upcoming Shows

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4831 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Screenrant

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Saying goodbye to 2026 also means the winter season is almost here.
  • While not all series releasing between December 2026 and February 2027 are included, we have previews for many of the biggest titles set to release in the coming months.
  • In a recent development, though streaming platforms such as Netflix, Prime Video, and Paramount+ will be frequently mentioned in this winter preview, we also have plenty to feature for fans of network TV.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Saying goodbye to 2026 also means the winter season is almost here. In the past, the fall used to be the most key season for TV, ushering in the year's biggest series, but that's no longer the case. Major TV shows release throughout the year, including the winter months, and ScreenRant is here with exclusive looks at more than 50 of those upcoming and returning titles coming in December, January, and February.

While not all series releasing between December 2026 and February 2027 are included, we have previews for many of the biggest titles set to release in the coming months. You will find titles linked to massive franchises like Star Wars, Marvel, One Piece, and even Garfield, as well as intriguing fresh series, spinoffs of past hits, long-awaited reboots, and a few Christmas specials.

In a recent development, though streaming platforms such as Netflix, Prime Video, and Paramount+ will be frequently mentioned in this winter preview, we also have plenty to feature for fans of network TV. In addition to highlights making their debut in early 2027, we also have exclusive looks at shows making their midseason returns this January.

Kicking off the December slate of latest releases on Netflix is a new thriller titled Trinity. The series centers on a naval commander (Gugu Mbatha-Raw) who gets pulled into a dangerous conspiracy tied to a top-secret program after becoming close to the Secretary of Defense (Richard Madden). Trinity comes from Jed Mercurio, the creator of Bodyguard, which also featured Madden in a lead role. The Netflix series also stars Marcia Gay Harden, JD Pardo, Bruce Greenwood, and James Remar in key roles.

Apple TV's comedy crime drama, Bad Monkey, is back for its sophomore season this December. Vince Vaughn returns as Andrew Yancy, the former detective who finds himself involved in another dangerous case between rival criminal organizations. In addition to dealing with a high-profile murder and a upcoming crime boss played by John Malkovich, Vaughn's character is also facing personal challenges with his father and romantic life. While the first season was based on Carl Hiaasen's novel, Bad Monkey season 2 is an original story.

Industry observers note that jane Austen's 1813 classic novel is getting a upcoming adaptation on Netflix with Pride and Prejudice. Arriving within the first few days of December, the limited series comes from writer Dolly Alderton and features a star-studded ensemble cast. While Emma Corrin and Jack Lowden will play leads, Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy, the rest of the cast includes names such as Olivia Colman, Rufus Sewell​​​, Louis Partridge, Freya Mavor, Fiona Shaw, and Daryl McCormack​​​​.

In a recent development, fraggle Rock was first rebooted on Apple TV in 2022, and the series is getting its third Christmas special to date with the release of Fraggle Rock: A Holiday Gift this December. When the holiday spirit starts to diminish in Fraggle Rock after a beloved snow globe is taken, Wembley, who is serving as the Fraggle in charge of holiday cheer, must step up to return it to its rightful owner. Fraggle Rock: A Holiday Gift will also feature a guest appearance by singer/actress Nicole Scherzinger​​​​.

Industry observers note that katori Hall's award-winning series P-Valley is finally back this December with nine episodes that will serve as the series' final installment. The Starz drama that last aired in 2022 is gearing up to say goodbye, but there's plenty of story left to tell for the residents of Chucalissa ​​​​​​and the drama that comes when a fresh casino opens in the area. While the casino will bring new faces, P-Valley season 3 will still be heavily focused on what's next for Uncle Clifford (Nicco Annan), Lil’ Murda (J. Alphonse Nicholson), Roulette (Gail Bean), Mercedes (Brandee Evans), and Keyshawn (Shannon Thornton).

Only Murders in the Building season 6 is going international, with Cinda Canning's (Tina Fey) murder sending Charles (Steve Martin), Oliver (Martin Short), and Mabel (Selena Gomez) to London for the investigation. Under the title of Only Murders in London for the upcoming installment, the hit Hulu series is embracing its new setting. Among season 6's guest stars are well-known UK figures, such as Olivia Colman, Simone Ashley, Nicola Coughlan, David Tennant, Jim Broadbent, Martin Freeman, Jodie Whittaker, and Geri Halliwell-Horner.

It has been revealed that maxton Hall - The World Between Us returns for its third and final season in early December with six brand-fresh episodes. The upcoming installment will follow Ruby (Harriet Herbig-Matten) dealing with the fallout of her suspension and affair scandal as her boyfriend James (Damian Hardung) helps set the record straight. The German romance series, which is based on Mona Kasten's novel Save Me, has been a global hit for Prime Video, and it looks like there will be plenty of drama for the show's concluding chapter.

Following the release of a Halloween special at the end of October, the supernatural sitcom is releasing another holiday-themed hour-long episode this December. The Ghosts Christmas special, titled Ghostmas: A Died Hard Special, releases on December 10, and it will be inspired by Die Hard, the 1988 action film that is still a topic of debate about whether it should be considered a Christmas movie. The episode will specifically see Utkarsh Ambudkar's Jay transform into the sitcom's version of John McClane after several ghosts are held hostage.

Traditional episodes for Ghosts season 6 will return January 21, 2027.

Industry observers note that based on the beloved comic strip by Jim Davis, Garfield is coming in the form of a new 2-D animated series on Paramount+. The show, co-produced by Nickelodeon Animation Studio, marks the first animated project for the franchise since Garfield and Friends concluded in 1994. In this new iteration, Lamorne Morris is voicing the sarcastic feline, with Joe Brogie taking on the voice of Jon Arbuckle. Aside from appearances by notable Garfield characters, like Odie, Arlene, and Nermal, the Paramount+ series will introduce plenty of newcomers.

It has been revealed that A new coming-of-age series titled Sunshine Girls is making its debut in mid-December on Netflix. The show will center on Alma Marian​​​​'s Olivia, a teen who makes the cross-country move from New York City to a California suburb following her parents' divorce. During her freshman year at a new school, Olivia quickly connects with classmates Taylor (Isabella Fowler) and Riley (Erin Rose Park), who happens to be an influencer. Speaking of influencers, Sunshine Girls will feature appearances by several real-life influencers, including Déjà Clark, PresLee Faith, Kaido Roberts, Kylie Castillo, and Nina Castillo.

It has been revealed that the reality competition series from Jimmy Donaldson, aka MrBeast, is returning for a third season this December on Prime Video. The season, titled Beast Games: World Champions, will feature competitors from around the globe, representing 196 nations, taking part in various challenges, giving one team a chance to win $5,000,000. Along with new challenges, Prime Video has also teased the Roman Colosseum global stage that was used for live audience members.

Recent findings suggest that freida Pinto stars in Netflix's upcoming family drama titled Unaccustomed Earth that follows a woman who moves her family from India to Cambridge, Massachusetts following a major cancer diagnosis. Not only does Parul Chaudhury (Pinto) return to a life she once sacrificed, but she also reconnects with a past lover, a relationship that ends up impacting her entire family. Unaccustomed Earth is notably based on a short story collection of the same name by author Jhumpa Lahiri and will also star Indraneil Sengupta, Iyla Sundarsingh McKaig, Siddharth​​​​​​, and Justin Bartha.

The next entry in the Ted franchise is coming this December with Ted: The Animated Series. The upcoming series serves as a sequel to the movies, taking place 12 years after the events of Ted 2. Though Ted and John both have their own families, they are still close friends and even live next door to each other. In addition to Seth MacFarlane returning to voice Ted, several members of the movies are back to voice their animated counterparts, including Mark Wahlberg (John), Amanda Seyfried (Sam), and Jessica Barth (Tami-Lynn). Peacock has also confirmed more episodes will debut in 2027.

Recent findings suggest that after making his debut in Tulsa King, Samuel L. Jackson's Russell Lee Washington Jr. is set to lead his own spinoff in Frisco King. While Taylor Sheridan has a history of developing spinoffs, Tulsa King is the first show outside the Yellowstone universe to get an expansion. The series, which also stars Asa Germann​​​, Kai Caster, Lilah Pate, and Savanna Gann, focuses on Russell trying to build a fresh criminal empire after relocating to Frisco, Texas. Sylvester Stallone's Tulsa King character, Dwight Manfredi, will also make an appearance.

Emily in Paris will bid adieu with the upcoming release of its sixth season, which will also be its last. The romantic comedy-drama first debuted in 2020 and turned into a lasting hit for the streamer. The final chapter slated to drop on Christmas Eve will see Lily Collins' Emily Cooper facing decisions that will shape her future from both a professional and personal standpoint after a trip to Greece results in a surprise run-in with Gabriel (Lucas Bravo). Emily in Paris season 6 will also see the return of major characters Mindy (Ashley Park), Sylvia (Philippine Leroy-Beaulieu), Lucien (Alfie), Princess Jane (Minnie Driver), Luc (Bruno Gouery), Julien (Samuel Arnold), and Antoine (William Abadie).

Industry observers note that prime Video's acclaimed docuseries One Night in Idaho is getting a three-part follow-up with the release of One Night in Idaho: Catching a Killer this December. Whereas the original docuseries focused on the four victims of the 2022 killings of University of Idaho students–Madison Mogen, Kaylee Goncalves, Ethan Chapin, and Xana Kernodle–the new episodes will follow the law enforcement officers who investigated the case, including Lead Detectives Brett Payne and Darren Gilbertson​​​​​.

The third season of Mayfair Witches, officially titled Anne Rice’s Mayfair Witches: Salem Coven, is making its debut by the end of the year. The latest installment shifts the setting to Salem, Massachusetts, after Alexandra Daddario Rowan Fielding finds herself stuck in the town best known for its long historical connection to witches. Salem Coven will also feature a few latest cast members, including Betsy Brandt, Michiel Huisman, Eliza Scanlen, James Frain, and Omar Maskati.

In a recent development, david Boreanaz is stepping into the role of James Rockford for NBC's The Rockford Files, coming this January. The reboot of the '70s crime drama follows a man tied to a crime he didn't commit, attempting to return to his job as a private investigator in Los Angeles. However, he's now a target of both the police and organized crime in the city. The series also stars Michaela McManus, Felix Solis, and Jacki Weaver.

Following the special preview on Saturday, January 2, The Rockford Files will return to its regular timeslot on January 7, 2027.

Will Trent is officially making its return as part of ABC's midseason schedule, beginning the first week of January. Season 5 picks back up following the deaths of Amanda Wagner (Sonja Sohn) and Dr. Seth McDale (Scott Foley), who also happens to be Angie's (Erika Christensen) husband. With a new baby, Will (Ramón Rodríguez) steps up to help the grieving mother, while newcomer Alexandra Metz joins the crime drama as Birdie Palmer, Amanda's successor as GBI Deputy Director.

Sources indicate that even though High Potential has a fresh showrunner, Kaitlin Olson's Morgan Gillory will still be at the front and center of ABC's hit comedy crime drama when it returns for season 3 in January. Though Steve Howey won't be returning as a lead character in the new installment, High Potential will still need to reveal Captain Wagner's fate following season 2's cliffhanger. That mentioned, there will be plenty of familiar faces sticking around, including Adam Karadec (Daniel Sunjata)​​​​​, Daphne Forrester (Javicia Leslie), Lev "Oz" Özdil (Deniz Akdeniz), and Lieutenant Selena Soto (Judy Reyes).

A special episode of High Potential season 3 will air following Super Bowl LXI on Sunday, February 14, 2027.

Shifting Gears is another popular ABC series making its grand return as part of the midseason slate. When season 2 ended, Kat Dennings' Riley found herself in a love triangle with Andy (Jesse Williams) and Gabe (Seann William Scott), something that will need to be resolved when the show picks back up with season 3. As for Riley's dad, Matt (Tim Allen), he's back together with Eve (Jenna Elfman), who will be appearing throughout the fresh installment. As for newcomers, Shifting Gears season 3 will feature a special 2 Broke Girls reunion when Beth Behrs makes a guest appearance as an ER doctor.

ABC's midseason schedule includes several of the network's most popular series, including The Rookie, which is set to return for its ninth season the first week of 2027. Nathan Fillion still leads the police procedural as John Nolan, but a lot of the attention coming into season 9 will be on the fates of Lucy Chen (Melissa O'Neil) and Tim Bradford (Eric Winter). As for newcomers in The Rookie season 9, it has been revealed that Troian Bellisario, Dulé Hill, and Molly Kunz will serve as guest stars.

2027 will notably see a double dose of The Rookie, with The Rookie: North making its official debut on January 6. The second spinoff of the original series follows Alex Holland (Jay Ellis), a middle-aged man who decides to join the police force after a life-altering home invasion. Though The Rookie: North is set in the Pacific Northwest, there's potential for future crossovers with the main series, especially with Nathan Fillion's character set to appear in the pilot.

Baywatch is getting the reboot-sequel ("requel") treatment at Fox, and the series is kicking off the first week of 2027. This new iteration is set to focus on original character Hobie Buchannon, who is now played by Stephen Amell, as he leads a group of LA lifeguards as the official Baywatch Captain. Hobie must also deal with the unexpected arrival of his biological daughter, Charlie (Jessica Belkin). Baywatch's cast also includes Hassie Harrison, Shay Mitchell, Brooks Nader, Noah Beck, Thaddeus LaGrone, and Livvy Dunn. Original Baywatch actors David Chokachi​​​​, Michael Bergin, Kelly Packard​​​, and Erika Eleniak will also appear.

Hugh Laurie stars in Apple TV's new crime thriller The Wanted Man as Felix Carmichael, a crime boss who finds himself in prison after being betrayed by a member of his own organization. In addition to seeking revenge on those who turned on him, Felix will also be looking to make a grand escape from prison to save his criminal empire. Debuting this January, The Wanted Man also stars Thandiwe Newton and is created by George Kay, who is also known for developing Lupin, Hijack, and HBO's recent War series.

Sources indicate that 9-1-1's midseason finale airs in November, but fans can already get ready for season 10's return. While we won't spoil what happens in "Et Tu?," the episode that serves as the fall finale, we can share a look at the show's return as part of ABC's big winter premiere week during the first week of January. The exclusive look features Ravi (Anirudh Pisharody) visiting May (Corinne Massiah) at the hospital where she works as part of her nursing program.

Following the midseason premiere of 9-1-1, the show's spinoff, 9-1-1: Nashville, will also return with a new episode as part of the sophomore season. Like the case with the main series, there's not much we can share regarding 9-1-1: Nashville season 2's return without spoiling the events of the fall finale, "Tears of the Nile." That said, we can provide an exclusive look at the future of season 2, specifically a new image of firefighters Blue (Hunter McVey) and Ryan (Michael Provost).

According to recent reports, november will also see the fall finale of Grey's Anatomy season 23, but that means it will join many other ABC titles in celebrating 2027 by returning the first week of January. The fall finale, "Till I Collapse," saw tension among Grey Sloan leadership when they did not agree on how to deal with a sudden increase in patients. As for what to expect when Grey's Anatomy season 23 returns, we have sneak peeks at Miranda Bailey (Chandra Wilson), Ben Warren (Jason George), Jules Millin (Adelaide Kane)​​​​​, Jo Wilson (Camilla Luddington), and Link (Chris Carmack).

According to recent reports, the Bosch franchise is growing yet again with a prequel series titled Bosch: Start of Watch. The series, which was first unveiled in late 2025, will star Cameron Monaghan as young Harry Bosch when he's still a rookie LA cop in 1992. Start of Watch will also introduce key figures that helped Harry's life earlier in his career, including a fellow rookie cop and potential love interest, Rosa (Ariana Guerra), and Harry's surrogate brother, Cory (JD Pardo). The MGM+ series has already been renewed for a second season.

Following on the heels of VisionQuest and Avengers: Doomsday, 2027 will see the arrival of Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man season 2 on Disney+. Though the animated series follows an alternate version of Peter Parker and Spider-Man, it's set within the multiverse, with season 2 specifically part of Phase 6 of the MCU. The new season will see Peter stuck between Norman Osborn and Doctor Ock's growing rivalry, as well as a bigger focus on the symbiote after the Venom story was teased in season 1.

Based on Ed Brubaker's comic book series of the same name, Criminal follows several families connected through generations of crime and secrets. The Prime Video series will release in two parts, "Coward" on January 13 and "Lawless" on January 27, with each part comprised of four episodes. "Coward" will center on Leo Patterson (Charlie Hunnam) and Ricky Lawless (Gus Halper), lifelong friends who can't run from a childhood murder and botched heist that pulls them right into their hidden past. Criminal's cast also includes Adria Arjona, Luke Evans, Emilia Clarke, Michael Mando, Garrett Hedlund, and Patrick J. Adams.

Following its debut in 2024, 3 Body Problem is back for season 2 in January. The sci-fi series based on Liu Cixin's novels confirmed the existence of an extraterrestrial civilization known as the San-Ti. In season 2, Earth is preparing for the San-Ti invasion with the plan to carry out a special space fleet mission that could be the only way to save the planet from being taken over. In addition to the return of cast members like Jovan Adepo, Liam Cunningham, Eiza González, Jess Hong, Benedict Wong, Sea Shimooka, Marlo Kelly, and Saamer Usmani, season 2 will see the arrival of Claudia Doumit​​​​​, Ellie de Lange​​​​​, and Alfie Allen, to name a few.

Industry observers note that taylor Sheridan's Mayor of Kingstown is nearing its end with the arrival of the show's fifth and final season on January 15. Led by Jeremy Renner in his role as Mike McLusky, Mayor of Kingstown season 5 will follow Mike and his brother Kyle looking for vengeance after the murder of Kyle's wife, Tracy. The death also brings FBI agent Russell Hardy (David Morse) to town, which complicates matters for the McLusky family. Aside from another newcomer played by Nestor Carbonell, season 5 will feature the return of Edie Falco, Lennie James, and, of course, Tobi Bamtefa as Deverin “Bunny” Washington​​​​​.

Miss Scarlet is another series coming to an end this winter after seven seasons. Debuting in mid-January, Miss Scarlet season 7 will feature Kate Phillips' Eliza take on her role as Victorian London's first female private detective as she balances a latest romance with Alexander Blake (Tom Durant-Pritchard) and a crime boss causing trouble in the city. Inspector Blake, on the other hand, will be dealing with his own career complications with a new superior officer at Scotland Yard.

It has been revealed that all Creatures Great and Small will also be making its seventh season debut this January on Masterpiece on PBS. The British series based on James Herriot’s novels is now focusing on Skeldale House and its team of veterinarians after the war in 1946. Spider-Noir Officially Returns After Prime Video Cancelled Nicolas Cage’s Series

💡 Key Takeaways
  • To say Spider-Noir's cancellation came as a shock would be an understatement.
  • Industry observers note that the silver lining is that Prime Video isn't done with Spider-Man.
  • During Latest York Comic Con, a whole new wave of Spider-Man comics was unveiled, including Spider-Man: Noir #1.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

To say Spider-Noir's cancellation came as a shock would be an understatement. Prime Video unleashed the hardboiled detective superhero hit to rave reviews earlier this year, earning a stellar 92% from critics on Rotten Tomatoes and five Emmy wins along the way for Best Cinematography, Sound Editing, Special Visual Effects, and more. Nicolas Cage's first regular television role also brought the star back into familiar territory as Ben Reilly, playing a similar but different role to that of his Spider-Verse character and giving life to the down-on-his-luck detective who stands as Fresh York's only superhero. Despite also finding success on the streaming charts, it ultimately wasn't enough to keep the story going, despite those involved having ideas for the future.

Industry observers note that the silver lining is that Prime Video isn't done with Spider-Man. Back in September, it was announced that a new series based on the Clone Saga was in the works, revolving around Ben Reilly and Kaine Parker and penned by American Born Chinese creator Kelvin Yu. It's born from the same overall deal between Amazon MGM Studios and Sony Pictures Television to create series based on Marvel characters, making it a sort of continuation of the wider universe Spider-Noir was a part of. For those who want more of the darker, detective-style stories, however, Marvel Comics will be the place to turn.

During Latest York Comic Con, a whole new wave of Spider-Man comics was unveiled, including Spider-Man: Noir #1. Penned by Alex Segura, who not only has worked within the Spider-Verse before but has authored his own award-winning mystery novel, Secret Identity, the issue will mark the beginning of a new chapter for the trenchcoat-wearing variant of Peter Parker as he dives back into the shadowy underworld. A new adversary awaits to quite literally drown him in darkness, all while he unravels the mystery surrounding his girlfriend's ex. In the end, the hero will be faced with a fateful decision that could decide his future, choosing between pursuing infinite power or catching a murderer on the loose. Farid Karami is handling the art, while Stephen Mooney will provide the cover.

Four powers, and four completely different kinds of person behind them. Here is what you would wake up with, what it would cost you, and why the MCU keeps handing it to somebody exactly like you.

You get the power that is really about taking the hit so that nobody else has to. Strength in the MCU always lands on people who were already carrying too much, which is exactly why it suits you.

You get the power that never switches off. Spider-sense is a gift and a nervous system on permanent alert, and the people who get it in these films are always the ones who were already worrying about everybody.

Sources indicate that you get the quietest power in the building, and quietly the most useful. Invisibility comes with force fields for a reason, because the people who prefer not to be seen are usually the ones holding a shield around everybody else.

According to recent reports, you get the biggest and least comfortable power on the list, the one that runs directly on feeling. Chaos magic is not really a superpower in the MCU so much as an emotional state with consequences attached.

In a recent development, perhaps the most exciting part about Segura's Spider-Man: Noir limited run is that it'll welcome Venom into the Noir universe. The symbiote has yet to appear in the hard-boiled Marvel world, so it's unknown what exactly Venom Noir could look like when it enters Peter's life. Readers will officially find out when the first matter hits store shelves on February 10, 2027. Segura teased in a statement to Marvel how the gritty tale will marry what he loves about the wider Spider-Man mythos with his favorite aspects of classic detective noir tales, wrestling with some of the themes that define Peter Parker as a character.

It has been revealed that “It’s been a treat to blend two of my favorite things — noir stories and the Spider-Man mythos — in the pages of Spider-Man Noir. Working with an amazing artist like Farid on a story that not only introduces mysterious (and perhaps familiar) elements to the Noir universe but also pushes Spidey to the brink has been a blast, and we’re aiming to keep readers on their toes from page one. Plus, we get to answer the ultimate question — can Peter Parker EVER be truly happy? Let’s find out.".

According to recent reports, stay tuned here at Collider for more on Marvel Comics' Spider-Man: Noir series as it nears. In the meantime, all episodes of Spider-Noir are available to stream on Prime Video.

How to Transfer Your Playlists to Tidal Music for Free

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (326 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I recently switched music streamers from Apple Music to Tidal.
  • Recent findings suggest that download your playlist as a .txt file.
  • Double click "install certificates" in the folder that opens after installation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I recently switched music streamers from Apple Music to Tidal. I like Tidal's strict anti-AI features, the fact that it pays higher royalties to artists than other major streamers, and its focus on high quality audio. I wrote a post featuring eight hacks for Tidal customers, but I wanted to highlight one in particular: How to transfer playlists without paying anything.

Recent findings suggest that download your playlist as a .txt file. You can do this directly from Apple Music under File>Library>Export Playlist. You can't from Spotify, but the free site Exportify will download any of your playlists as a spreadsheet file you can save.

Install Python on your system. Double click "install certificates" in the folder that opens after installation.

Sources indicate that download this script. Save it in the same file as your playlist.

Run the script: (For Mac, open Terminal. For Windows, go to the Command prompt. Type python3 on a Mac or py on Windows.) Drag the script into the terminal window and press enter. It should ask you to drag your downloaded playlist into the window next.

Industry observers note that sign in to Tidal. Hit "Approve" to give permission for Tidal to run the script.

In a recent development, have a banana. The script is going to search for all the songs on your playlist and match them to Tidal's library, so it can take a little while. I tested it with a playlist from Apple Music with 2,397 songs. It took about 20 minutes and found 2,362 of my tracks, a 99% success rate.

Fix the leftovers: The program creates two separate text files for "orphans." One is songs it couldn't find and one is songs it might be worth double-checking manually.

If everything goes well, your large playlist should be available on Tidal.

Note: The script uses a community-created library to talk to Tidal, so it could stop working if Tidal changes things up.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’ve been holding off on picking up a TV or upgrading your current set, you absolutely made the right move as Black Friday is without a doubt, the best time to get a fresh TV. From Best Buy to Walmart, practically every retailer has Black Friday TV deals worth checking out.

Whether you want more screen size for what you’d normally pay for something a lot smaller, an OLED panel for deeper blacks or just a fresh TV with all the latest features, there’s something for every living room and every budget.

Let’s say you blueprint on putting your TV in a bright room with a lot of ambient light. In that case, you might want to invest in an art TV with a glare-free screen that doubles as a digital canvas. For instance, you can pick up the Samsung 65-inch The Frame Pro Neo QLED 4K TV for $1,499 at Best Buy or even the Amazon 55-inch Ember Artline 4K QLED TV for $499 at Amazon.

According to recent reports, I’ve had my eyes on an art TV for a while now but if you want an OLED or QLED TV to use in a darker room, there are even more Black Friday TV deals that are live right now when you scroll down below. For more deals, check out our full Black Friday deals guide.

In a recent development, the Ember Artline is Amazon’s first art TV and if you’re looking for a smaller set, you can pick this one up at its lowest price yet. It features a matte 4K QLED display and when you’re not watching something using its Fire TV interface, you can have it act as artwork. Amazon’s Ember Artline TVs also come with Alexa+ built-in so you can ask questions about what’s on the display or even control your smart home right from your TV.

This 65-inch TV from Hisense hits the sweet spot in terms of size and features. The E7 has a Hi-QLED panel with Mini-LED backlighting to enhance contrast and bring details to life. You’re also getting a native 144Hz high refresh rate game mode which is perfect for console or even PC gaming on the big screen. Powered by Amazon’s Fire TV OS, the E7 also packs in Dolby Vision Atmos and AI picture upscaling.

Industry observers note that now if you want a more feature-rich art TV, Hinsense’s S7 Canvas TV is the better pick over Amazon’s Ember Artline. This TV has a faster 144Hz refresh rate and comes with Google TV built-in. In addition to a frame, you also get an ultra slim wall mount in the box. As for art, you get access to over 1,000 curated works but you can also display your own photos and collections too.

TCL’s A400U is more of a hybrid than a typical art TV since it doesn’t come with a frame. You still get an HVA Pro Panel to help fight off glare and access to built-in art for when your TV is idle though. The A400U also has a super slim 1.57-inch profile and with the included mounting bracket, this TV sits just 0.12-inch away from your wall when installed. It also has a 144Hz refresh rate and 836 dimming zones with up to HDR 2500 nits of brightness.

With over 8 million self-lit pixels in its OLED panel, the Sony Bravia 6 delivers pure blacks and stunning contrast. Powered by Google TV, this OLED TV also packs in Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos and four HDMI 2.1 ports. The Sony Bravia 6 is a great TV for watching films and TV shows as well as playing games thanks to its 120 Hz refresh rate at 4K. This isn’t the only model that’s on sale either and you can go all the way down to 48 inches or all the way up to 83 inches too.

In a recent development, samsung RG85H Micro RGB TV uses fresh red, green and blue LEDs instead of just traditional white ones for better color volume. This works regardless of what you’re watching too thanks to the TV’s built-in Micro RGB AI engine. Powered by Samsung’s Tizen platform, you also get a 144 Hz refresh rate and variable refresh rate (VRR) tech along with AMD FreeSync Premium Pro for extra smooth gameplay.

It has been revealed that the Samsung S90H features a glare-free OLED display without sacrificing brightness. In fact, in our Samsung S90H OLED TV review, we praised its LCD-like brightness, better-than-expected audio and top gaming capabilities. This is a great TV for gaming as it comes with four HDMI 2.1 ports for 4K gaming at 120 Hz (and up to 165 Hz) and comes with FreeSync Premium Pro as well as G-Sync compatibility. In addition to this 65-inch model, you can also find the 42, 48, 55, 77 and 83-inch ones on sale too.

Industry observers note that the C6 is LG's flagship OLED TV for 2026. In our LG C6 OLED TV review we said the Editor's Choice TV performs brilliantly offering top-tier brightness and colors. We're also fans of its gameplay enhancing features including a latest Game Optimizer mode that obliterates input lag and boosts FPS on both consoles and PCs. It's predecessor, the C5, is still a great TV and cheaper, but if you want the latest and greatest — you won't be disappointed with the C6.

Sources indicate that the Frame Pro takes Samsung’s tried and true The Frame art TVs to the next level with mini-LED backlighting, Samsung Vision AI and up to 4K gaming at 144Hz. You’re still getting a glare-free, matte display and of course, art mode. With Samsung’s Wireless One Connect box, you don’t have to run any cables up to the TV on the wall either. Instead, you’ll just have to hide its power cable.

The QM7L is TCL’s first Super Quantum Dot (SQD) TVs and as a result, it offers better contrast and color than other Mini-LED TVs. In fact, we were so impressed with it, we crowned the QM7L the best mini-LED TV in this year’s Tom’s Guide Awards. While the 55, 65 and 75 versions of this TV are also on sale, this deal gets you an impressive TV with one of the biggest screens you can get.

#39508. Industry News: Eight Notable Router Settings You Should Check (or Change)

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (709 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Eight Notable Router Settings You Should Check (or Change)

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (709 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Your router is a key piece of your home network, as it connects all of your other devices to the internet.
  • Industry observers note that your router's security protocol determines how encryption and authentication work to protect data that's transmitted over your network.
  • According to recent reports, some routers ship with factory default login credentials, which are the username and password you need to access your device's admin dashboard.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your router is a key piece of your home network, as it connects all of your other devices to the internet. This also makes it a highly valuable target for attackers and can leave your data vulnerable—especially if you simply plug your router in with its default settings unchanged. Whether your router is brand latest or it's been a while since you audited your existing setup, these are the key settings to check and change right now.

Industry observers note that your router's security protocol determines how encryption and authentication work to protect data that's transmitted over your network. WPA3 Personal is the newest standard and the most secure, so if it's available on your router, enable it. It's compatible with devices that support Wi-Fi 6. Some older devices may not work with WPA3, in which case the WPA2/WPA3 Transitional mixed mode is a good alternative. At minimum, set your router to WPA2 Personal (AES).

According to recent reports, some routers ship with factory default login credentials, which are the username and password you need to access your device's admin dashboard. (This is not the same as your network name or wifi password, which you set up later.) Default router passwords are searchable online, which leaves your router's admin settings open to anyone. Once you get into your dashboard for the first time, change the default credentials and enable two-factor authentication for your admin account if available.

While some newer routers do have unique, device-specific defaults, it's a good idea to check this setting and ensure it's secure. If you're prompted to create custom admin credentials during the setup process, do it.

Industry observers note that your network name, or SSID, is how your network appears when you search for available wifi. By default, this may be the name of the router brand or a short string of characters, but you should choose something unique to your network. Make sure there's no identifying personal information, such as your name or house number. While you may be tempted to hide your network and obscure your SSID, this may actually make your information less secure, so keep this setting disabled. You can, however, add "_nomap" to the end of your network name, which prevents your router's physical coordinates from being mapped by location databases.

It has been revealed that the password to access your network should also be unique and secure and should not include obvious personal information. One option to keep it memorable and easy to type is to create a passphrase using five to seven unrelated words that, combined, have at least 16 characters.

Sources indicate that two additional settings that leave your network vulnerable are Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) and Universal Plug and Play (UPnP). The former lets consumers connect to your network with a PIN, which can be vulnerable to brute-force attacks. The latter allows smart devices to easily connect to your network—but this also allows malware to spread more readily. You may need to have UPnP on in order to connect devices initially but should disable it afterward.

Sources indicate that any easy win for your network security is segmenting traffic to different networks, so if one is compromised, the data on the others remain unaffected. Many wifi routers have a "guest mode," which creates a separate SSID and password that you can share with visitors instead of giving them your primary network credentials. You can also set up a separate network for all of your smart home and IoT devices so exploitable vulnerabilities in these devices don't put your computers, phones, and other connected devices at risk too.

It has been revealed that routers run a type of software—called firmware—just like any other device. Firmware controls the router's core functions and is not immune to vulnerabilities, which can be exploited by bad actors. And, just like other types of software, manufacturers occasionally push updates to patch these flaws. Check your router's dashboard to see if automatic updates are toggled on. Some devices require an opt-in for auto updates during setup, so you should enable them if they are off. Some routers may even require manual updates—in this case, set a monthly or quarterly (at minimum) calendar reminder to check for patches.

#39506. 8 Movies Guy Ritchie Almost Directed But Never Made, Including Sherlock Holmes 3

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1412 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Screenrant ↗ Open Full Page

8 Movies Guy Ritchie Almost Directed But Never Made, Including Sherlock Holmes 3

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1412 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Screenrant

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Guy Ritchie has built a career around fast-talking criminals, elaborate schemes, and action sequences that rarely unfold as expected.
  • According to recent reports, over the years, Ritchie has been attached to several high-profile movies that ultimately moved forward without him or never reached the screen.
  • Not every abandoned project represents a missed opportunity, especially when another director eventually delivers a successful movie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Guy Ritchie has built a career around fast-talking criminals, elaborate schemes, and action sequences that rarely unfold as expected. After making his name with British crime movies like Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels and Snatch, he made his way into major Hollywood productions. While Guy Ritchie's filmography spans several genres, some of the movies he was attached to direct could have taken his career in entirely different directions.

According to recent reports, over the years, Ritchie has been attached to several high-profile movies that ultimately moved forward without him or never reached the screen. While some seemed like natural fits for his filmmaking style, others offered opportunities to explore newly introduced genres.

Not every abandoned project represents a missed opportunity, especially when another director eventually delivers a successful movie. However, several of Ritchie's unrealized films give an interesting glimpse at the creative directions he considered pursuing. Some have remained stuck in development for years, while others underwent substantial changes after he departed. From crime thrillers and comic book adaptations to a long-awaited return for Sherlock Holmes, these eight movies demonstrate how much of a director's career can be shaped by the films that never happen.

Guy Ritchie helped reinvent Sherlock Holmes for modern audiences with 2009's Sherlock Holmes, starring Robert Downey Jr. as the brilliant detective and Jude Law as his partner, Dr. John Watson. Ritchie's interpretation combined Holmes' sharp intellect with stylized action scenes, quick-witted exchanges, and an entertaining dynamic between the detective and Watson. He continued this approach in 2011's Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows, which brought Holmes face-to-face with his greatest adversary, Professor Moriarty, played by Jared Harris.

Industry observers note that however, Ritchie never returned for the planned third installment. In 2019, Rocketman director Dexter Fletcher was announced as his replacement, but the sequel subsequently encountered numerous delays. Interestingly, Ritchie hasn't ruled out returning to the franchise. During a May 2026 interview, he expressed interest in making another Sherlock Holmes movie, although his involvement remains unconfirmed. If Ritchie does return, the third film could recapture the elements between Holmes and Watson that made his first two installments so entertaining.

Industry observers note that after directing Disney's successful live-action Aladdin remake in 2019, Guy Ritchie was set to tackle another animated classic. In June 2022, Disney tapped him to direct a live-action adaptation of 1997's Hercules, which follows the son of Zeus as he attempts to reclaim his place among the gods. Unlike Aladdin, which largely followed the original film's story, the proposed Hercules remake appeared to be taking a different approach.

Joe and Anthony Russo, who were producing the film through their AGBO manufacturer, told Variety that they envisioned a more experimental musical influenced by modern audiences and TikTok. However, the project has struggled to gain momentum. Ritchie was reportedly no longer directing the remake by January 2024, although the Russo brothers subsequently indicated that he remained involved. His current status is unclear, and as of late 2026, Disney has yet to announce an official cast or release date (via People).

Industry observers note that guy Ritchie nearly reunited with Jake Gyllenhaal for Road House 2, the planned sequel to Amazon MGM Studios' 2024 action remake (via TheWrap). Directed by Doug Liman, the first film starred Gyllenhaal as Dalton, a former UFC fighter hired to work as a bouncer at a Florida Keys bar. However, Dalton soon finds himself fighting off a group of criminals determined to drive the bar's owner out of business.

In April 2025, Ritchie was revealed as the sequel's director, setting up a reunion with Gyllenhaal after their collaboration on 2023's The Covenant. Having previously directed action-heavy crime films like The Gentlemen and Wrath of Man, Ritchie seemed like a natural fit for the project. However, he exited the sequel just three months later, with no official explanation for his departure (via TheWrap). Nobody director Ilya Naishuller took over, and the film has since completed production.

Sources indicate that before returning to Sherlock Holmes, Guy Ritchie was preparing to direct a live-action adaptation of DC Comics' Lobo (via Variety). The character is an alien bounty hunter known for his violent tendencies, dark humor, and love of motorcycles. In September 2009, Warner Bros. announced Ritchie as director, with a script by Don Payne. The proposed film would have followed Lobo to Earth as he hunted four dangerous fugitives. Given Ritchie's work with volatile criminals like Brick Top in Snatch (2000), Lobo's brutality and unpredictable behavior could have been a great fit for his darkly comedic approach to violence.

Recent findings suggest that however, the success of 2009's Sherlock Holmes changed Warner Bros.' priorities. In January 2010, producer Joel Silver told the Los Angeles Times that the studio wanted Ritchie to focus on a sequel rather than Lobo. Ritchie then directed 2011's Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows, while his proposed DC adaptation was never developed.

Layer Cake (2004) seemed like an obvious fit for Guy Ritchie, especially after Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels and Snatch. Like those films, it explores London's criminal underworld, but its protagonist approaches business differently. Daniel Craig plays an unnamed cocaine dealer who treats drug trafficking like a legitimate profession, avoiding unnecessary violence and trouble. Just as he's preparing to retire, his boss gives him two final assignments that threaten to unravel his carefully controlled life.

Matthew Vaughn, who produced both Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels and Snatch, originally developed Layer Cake for Ritchie to direct (via Phase9). When Ritchie passed on the project, Vaughn decided to direct it himself. His version took a more restrained approach than Ritchie's earlier crime films, focusing on Craig's performance and the escalating consequences of his character's decisions. Layer Cake marked Vaughn's directorial debut, followed by films such as Kick-Ass and Kingsman: The Secret Service.

Sgt. Rock would have taken Guy Ritchie into a different corner of the DC universe. Rather than dealing with superheroes or supervillains, the film would have followed Frank Rock, a World War II infantry sergeant who leads a unit known as Easy Organization. The character's stories focus on ordinary soldiers fighting their way through dangerous missions, often under overwhelming odds. Ritchie was linked to an adaptation that would have kept the original wartime setting, with Bruce Willis reportedly considered for the lead role. Given his experience with ensemble casts, the soldiers' competing personalities could have been an interesting part of his version.

It has been revealed that ritchie's version ultimately fell through, and by 2009, Warner Bros. had brought in Francis Lawrence to develop a new adaptation set in the future rather than World War II (via Los Angeles Times). Ritchie was reportedly reconsidered in 2011, but he never returned as director. Decades of attempts to bring Sgt. Rock to the screen have followed, including a version from Luca Guadagnino that was shelved in April 2025 (via TheWrap). However, DC Studios co-CEO James Gunn subsequently confirmed that the project was still being considered, just without Guadagnino attached.

A pirate adventure might seem like a departure for Guy Ritchie, but the betrayals and double-crosses in Robert Louis Stevenson's Treasure Island have plenty in common with his earlier crime films. The story follows Jim Hawkins, a young boy who discovers a treasure map and joins an expedition in search of buried gold. Among the crew is Long John Silver, who earns Jim's trust while secretly planning a mutiny. Silver's shifting loyalties would have fit naturally into one of Ritchie's stories, where even the most charming characters often have their own agendas.

Industry observers note that in June 2012, Warner Bros. attached Ritchie to direct a fresh adaptation, with Alex Harakis writing the screenplay. The studio reportedly envisioned a stylized action blockbuster similar to Ritchie's Sherlock Holmes films. However, his version never reached production, and no official reason for its disappearance was revealed.

It has been revealed that the Dirty Dozen (1967) stars Lee Marvin as Major John Reisman, an officer tasked with turning 12 convicted soldiers into a unit capable of carrying out a dangerous mission behind enemy lines. Their constant fighting and disregard for authority create nearly as many problems as the mission itself.

Sources indicate that guy Ritchie was linked to a remake in 2007 alongside producer Joel Silver and publicly expressed interest in directing it. However, the film never moved forward. David Ayer was later brought in to develop a different version, leaving the original remake plans involving Guy Ritchie unmade.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27.3 beta 2 is now available, and Apple is adding the ability for customers to unlock higher usage limits for Apple Intelligence and Siri AI via iCloud+. Here’s everything you need to know.

From the start, Apple has said that some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features have usage limits because “they rely on powerful server models.” The organization previously outlined that increased access would be available across most iCloud+ subscription looks, and now we have the full details on how this will work.

Apple indicates the new system applies to several categories of Apple Intelligence features, including:.

The usage limits are per device, not per account. This means your iPhone, iPad, and Mac each have separate allowances. Apple isn’t disclosing specific limit numbers. Instead, it says that limits can vary based on the feature, request complexity, system demand, and more.

According to recent reports, as you near your limit, you’ll see an alert within whichever feature you’re using. For example, if you are using Image Playground, a message will appear telling you that you’ve almost hit your usage limit for the day. Once you hit the limit, you’ll be prompted to wait for it to reset or upgrade your iCloud+ blueprint.

Recent findings suggest that if you hit your limit, basic Siri requests will still work. This includes things like setting timers and alarms. Requests that require Siri to understand personal context and perform more complex, multi-step actions, however, are subject to the limits.

For example, asking Siri to find the details of an upcoming dinner reservation in your email and add them to your calendar would count toward your daily limit.

Additionally, each device uses its own standard daily usage limit first. After that, it can tap into the additional capacity included with an eligible iCloud+ subscription:.

It has been revealed that the usage unlocked by iCloud+ is shared across all devices signed in to your Apple Account, as well as family members sharing your iCloud+ initiative. The shared usage is available on a first-come, first-served basis.

It has been revealed that all limits will reset daily at the same time, and limits don’t roll over. In most cases, limits reset around midnight in your current time zone.

Apple has published a support document with more details.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that rewatching the original “The Hunger Games” this week before seeing the latest prequel “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,” I was struck by how much Jennifer Lawrence’s powerful, empathetic performance carries what is otherwise a fairly generic dystopian game-of-death movie. If “The Hunger Games” is operating on a slightly higher level than other similar movies, that’s almost entirely thanks to Lawrence’s compelling performance as Katniss Everdeen, the steely teenager who eventually leads a rebellion against the tyrannical government of Panem.

It has been revealed that as has been widely reported, Lawrence shows up again in “Sunrise on the Reaping,” although her appearance is so brief that it hardly makes an impression. Instead, the movie focuses on relative newcomer Joseph Zada as Haymitch Abernathy, the character played as an adult by Woody Harrelson in the first four “Hunger Games” movies. Like the 2023 prequel “The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes,” the new movie suffers from its lack of a Lawrence-caliber star who can hold the audience’s attention through yet another iteration of the overly familiar titular tournament.

It has been revealed that directed by Francis Lawrence, who helmed four of the previous five “Hunger Games” movies, “Sunrise on the Reaping” is competently produced and occasionally exciting, with an admirably downbeat finale. But it’s hard to shake the feeling that it’s entirely redundant, filling in gaps that didn’t need to be filled, just for the sake of returning to the world of an enduringly popular franchise.

Set 24 years before the events of “The Hunger Games,” “Sunrise on the Reaping” follows Haymitch as he competes in the 50th annual edition of the event that pits children from the 12 districts of Panem against each other in a gruesome death match. This year’s edition, known as the second “quarter quell,” requires each district to send twice as many tributes as usual, so Haymitch is joined by three others from his home in District 12.

Haymitch is a headstrong rebel who’s picked for the Hunger Games not by chance, but because he dared to stick up for his girlfriend, Lenore Dove Baird (Whitney Peak), when she was being roughed up by the militaristic Peacekeepers. One of Lenore Dove’s favorite things to say is that nothing is inevitable, but anyone who’s seen the previous “Hunger Games” movies knows that it actually is inevitable that Haymitch will win the Hunger Games, and that he won’t be able to topple Panem’s totalitarian regime.

Recent findings suggest that that takes a lot of the suspense out of “Sunrise on the Reaping,” even though author Suzanne Collins (who adapts her book along with screenwriters Billy Ray and Michael Lesslie) finds ways to generate excitement along the way to the predetermined outcome. Haymitch teams up with younger versions of some recognizable characters, including previous Hunger Games winners, to attempt to sabotage the games, and his path to victory isn’t straightforward or simple.

Still, much of the movie involves the same kind of battles and threats that Katniss faced multiple times in the earlier installments.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Like “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes,” which takes place during the 10th Hunger Games and provides an origin story for Panem’s diabolical President Coriolanus Snow (played here by Ralph Fiennes), “Sunrise on the Reaping” fills in some details on the history of Panem, including the evolution of the Hunger Games themselves.

Sources indicate that lawrence gives this time period a 1970s feel, with lots of wide-lapel outfits and groovy upholstery patterns, and the Hunger Games are not quite as sophisticated as in Katniss’ era, although much more so than in the more distant past. The setting allows Collins to embrace the brutality of the dystopian world while preserving the hopeful ending of the original four movies.

Zada is a bit bland as Haymitch, but he captures enough of Harrelson’s vocal mannerisms that the two versions of the character feel connected. The other younger incarnations of existing characters are a mixed bag, from Kieran Culkin’s failure to channel Stanley Tucci’s effortless smarm as host Caesar Flickerman to Elle Fanning’s uncanny recreation of Elizabeth Banks’ flamboyant stylist Effie Trinket.

Some of those appearances are little more than fan service, but they give the sense of Panem as a wider society, beyond Katniss’ personal connections. Longtime fans may be satisfied just to spend more time in Panem, but “Sunrise on the Reaping” rarely establishes itself as a distinctive story worth telling on its own.

The only time when “Sunrise on the Reaping” has any bite is in its extended epilogue, after the Hunger Games have concluded. That’s when the true price that Haymitch has to pay becomes clear, and the filmmakers don’t hold back on torturing the young man who’s already been through such a horrific ordeal. It’s the same darkness that defined the final hour of “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes,” here focused on a character more deserving of sympathy.

That bracing sorrow comes only after nearly two hours of the Hunger Games’ greatest hits, and it doesn’t make as much of an impact as it could, given what viewers know about Haymitch’s ultimate fate. That’s the problem with any prequel, and “Sunrise on the Reaping” never quite overcomes it. Even when their storytelling faltered, the original “Hunger Games” movies always had Jennifer Lawrence to fall back on. By the time she finally shows up here, there’s not much she can do.

“The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” opens Nov. 20 in theaters.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that apple is at the moment beta testing the third major update in the iOS 27 era, and anyone—developer and public tester alike—is free to install it at their leisure.
  • Industry observers note that with the second iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple is introducing face unlock for the iPhone Duo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple dropped iOS 27.2.1 last week, patching a handful of security vulnerabilities and bugs—including two iMessage flaws that let people read messages they shouldn't. But while most of us are running this version (or should install it as soon as possible), others are running something different—iOS 27.3.

Recent findings suggest that apple is at the moment beta testing the third major update in the iOS 27 era, and anyone—developer and public tester alike—is free to install it at their leisure. With it, comes the return of the Health app, vertical Safari tabs, and Siri AI app actions, among other new features. But for people of Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, iOS 27.3 brings two rather notable changes—both of which are for the better.

Industry observers note that with the second iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple is introducing face unlock for the iPhone Duo. The foldable famously ships with Touch ID, the first new iPhone since the third-gen iPhone SE to do so. While that isn't a problem per se, many of us are used to unlocking our iPhones with our faces. This update just lets new Duo owners keep up with that muscle memory.

Now, take note: This isn't Face ID. No software upgrade can introduce newly introduced hardware, so the iPhone Duo still doesn't have the camera tech required to power Apple's Face ID system. As such, the Duo's face unlock is likely not as secure as Face ID on other iPhones. Perhaps that's why your iPhone Duo will require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. This feature seems to be one of pure convenience: If you want to be able to unlock your Duo with your face (at least, some of the time), you can.

It has been revealed that what's more, this isn't a default setting. If you're running the beta, or if you're reading this after iOS 27.3 drops, you can find the option in Settings > Touch ID & Passcode.

Apple made a major deal about the continuity involved with opening and closing the iPhone Duo. As you do, your content moves with you seamlessly—a very Apple thing to do. That stated, you might expect folding the Duo to lock it, but it doesn't. You need to hit the side button to actually put the phone to sleep.

According to recent reports, iOS 27.3 changes that. If you so choose, you can enable a setting to lock your Duo whenever you close it. That won't work for everyone, of course—some people may still want to move between modes without worrying about locking their Duos. But for those who would rather lock their devices whenever they fold them up, the upcoming option is under Settings > Display & Brightness.
