📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Film Committee at Media City Qatar has signed a memorandum of understanding with UAE-based regional streaming service Yango Play to explore the development, co-production and distribution of scripted and unscripted Arabic-language originals.

The accord, declared on the sidelines of the Film Committee at Media City Qatar’s Doha Industry Days 2026, will also cover content acquisition and licensing opportunities, kicking off with eight-part Qatari documentary series Elzam.

Produced by Doha-based Katara Studios, the series explores the Gulf region tradition of falconry through a group of contemporary falconers. It with premiere with the screening of a special episode at the Doha Film Festival, running alongside the Industry Days. Related Stories Festivals Qatar's Film Committee Head Hassan Al-Thawadi Teases 2nd Industry Days In Doha: "We Are moving From Vision To Execution" News Festival In Focus: Qatar Ramps Up International Film & TV Ambitions As Local Talent Shines.

Sources indicate that yango Play will seek to bring the series to audiences across the region and beyond the Middle East and North Africa. Watch on Deadline.

“Our ambition is to build a sustainable screen industry in Qatar that creates lasting opportunities for Arabic-language productions and Qatari and regional talent,” said Hassan Al Thawadi, Chairman of the Film Committee at Media City Qatar.

“Via our partnership with Yango Play, we will explore ways to develop original Arabic-language productions, build expertise within Qatar’s production sector and bring stories from across the Arab world to international audiences.”.

Yango Play is an entertainment App offering video streaming, music, and mini-games and integrated with the Yasmina AI assistant. It was launched in 2024 and has a special focus on Arabic-language content, with its biggest audiences in the Gulf and Egypt.

“Our partnership with the Film Committee at Media City Qatar represents an vital opportunity to champion Arabic storytelling and support the creative talent shaping the region’s entertainment industry,” stated Roman Shimanskiy, Chief Executive of Yango Play and Yasmina.

“Together, we look forward to exploring fresh collaborations that bring compelling local stories to life, create opportunities for regional talent and connect Qatari and regional productions with audiences across MENA and beyond.”.

Industry observers note that the Nothing Headphone (a) is down to a record-low $109 from $199, making it a solid option for everyday listening, especially for Android people who can take advantage of LDAC for higher-quality wireless audio. For more on it, check out this PCMag review.

In a recent development, spending another $60 gets you the Nothing Headphone (1), now $169 from $299, which is also a record low. It offers a more premium listening experience with active noise cancellation, automatic playback pausing when you take the headphones off, and the option to listen through either USB-C or a 3.5mm cable, making it a well-rounded choice for everyday use. For more on it, check out this PCMag review.

Nothing's newest and most expensive over-ears, the Headphone (1) Pro, are already $80 off at $319, only a couple of months after launching at $399. This is the pair to get for sound quality, since Nothing moved to a three-driver setup in each earcup, and the result is a fuller, more detailed sound than either the Headphone (1) or Headphone (a). For more on it, check out this PCMag review.

Sony's flagship WH-1000XM6 headphones are down to $378 from $459.99, their lowest price yet. Noise cancellation is still the main reason to buy them, and they remain among the best options for blocking out engine rumble on a flight, traffic during a commute, or chatter in a busy office. For more on these over-ears, you can check out our in-depth review.

Sony's WH-CH730N brings noise cancellation down to a much more approachable price, and at $98, down from $179.99, it's the lowest it's been on Amazon.
